brief: Three 20 mm PLA balls in a row, their centres 15 mm apart, fused into one piece. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

intent.summary: A decorative or placeholder piece consisting of three equal spheres fused in a row, explicitly stated to carry no load.
stated: The balls are fused into one piece
It carries no load, so there is no load case
implied: Since centre spacing (15 mm) is less than ball diameter (20 mm), the balls must overlap/intersect, implying the fused geometry is a continuous blended solid rather than balls touching at a point
Fused into one piece implies a single solid body (manifold) is expected as output, not three separate assembled parts
PLA as material implies this is likely for FDM 3D printing, suggesting build orientation/support considerations may matter even without load
unstated: Whether the three centres lie on a straight line and their exact alignment/axis orientation
The amount or style of blending/fillet at the ball intersections (sharp intersection vs smooth fillet)
Overall orientation of the row in space (for printing or mounting)
Any functional use case (toy, fidget object, test print, display piece) that might affect tolerances even if not load-bearing
Whether any mounting feature, hole, or attachment point is needed despite 'no load' claim
Dimensional tolerances for the 20 mm diameter and 15 mm spacing
Expected print orientation or minimum wall/infill requirements if hollowed
out_of_scope: Structural load analysis (explicitly excluded by brief)
risk_signals: None apparent: brief explicitly states no load is carried and describes a simple decorative fused-ball form with no indication of human-carrying, pressure containment, stored energy, or vehicle/regulated-equipment use

requirements.statement: The fused row of three balls shall span 50 mm end to end along the row axis (two 15 mm centre spacings plus one ball radius at each end).
requirements.rationale: Three centres 15 mm apart, each ball 20 mm diameter (10 mm radius): outer extent = 2*15 + 20 = 50 mm.

requirements.statement: The part's extent perpendicular to the row shall equal one ball's diameter, 20 mm.
requirements.rationale: With centres collinear, the widest cross-section anywhere is a single ball's diameter.

requirements.statement: The part's extent perpendicular to the row shall equal one ball's diameter, 20 mm.
requirements.rationale: Same reasoning as Y: a row of equal collinear spheres has identical extent in both directions normal to its axis.

requirements.statement: Each of the three balls shall be 20 mm in diameter.
The centres of adjacent balls shall be spaced 15 mm apart.
The part shall consist of exactly three spherical balls fused together.

assumptions.statement: The three ball centres lie on a single straight line (a collinear row), not a bent or offset arrangement.
assumptions.rationale: The brief says 'in a row,' which conventionally means collinear centres.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If the row is meant to bend or offset, the bounding box and overlap geometry would change, but the part would still read as three fused balls.

assumptions.statement: The balls are fused by a plain boolean union (natural intersection curve between overlapping spheres), with no additional fillet or blend added at the junctions.
assumptions.rationale: The brief only says 'fused into one piece,' which a union of overlapping spheres (15 mm spacing < 20 mm diameter, so they already overlap) naturally satisfies.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: A smoother blended fillet would look different but the overall envelope, diameters and spacing would be unaffected.

assumptions.statement: The row of balls is modelled lying along the part's X axis.
assumptions.rationale: The brief gives no orientation; X is an arbitrary but conventional choice for a linear feature's long axis.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: A different axis choice only relabels which bounding-box slot (X vs Y) carries the 50 mm figure; it does not change the part's actual shape.

document.name: three_ball_chain
document.description: Three equal spheres fused into a single body, centres collinear along X at 15 mm spacing; decorative, non-structural.

parameters.description: Diameter of each of the three fused balls
Centre-to-centre distance between adjacent balls along the row axis

answer.rationale: Three sphere primitives (each tagged "ball" for the feature-count requirement) placed with centres collinear along X at -centre_spacing, 0, +centre_spacing, each sharing the single ball_diameter parameter so all three stay equal and the spacing stays parametric. A plain union (no blend_radius, per the no-extra-fillet assumption) fuses them into the single terminal solid; since spacing (15 mm) < diameter (20 mm) the spheres already overlap, giving a continuous manifold body with 50 mm X extent and 20 mm Y/Z extent as required.

note: Three balls in a row were held to 'as wide in every direction' (0.4): Forge read 'balls' as the part being a ball.
